\label{lemma-shriek-proper-and-open}
Consider a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
with $f$ and $f'$ proper and $g$ and $g'$ separated and locally quasi-finite.
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring. Functorially in $K \in D(X'_\etale, \Lambda)$
there is a canonical map
$$
g_!Rf'_*K \longrightarrow Rf_*(g'_!K)
$$
in $D(Y_\etale, \Lambda)$. This map is an isomorphism if
(a) $K$ is bounded below and has torsion cohomology sheaves, or
(b) $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring.
statement: Consider a **commutative** (not necessarily Cartesian) square of schemes $X'\xrightarrow{g'}X$, $X'\xrightarrow{f'}Y'$, $X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, $Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, where $f,f'$ are proper and $g,g'$ separated locally quasi-finite. For a ring $\Lambda$ and any $K\in D(X'_{\acute et},\Lambda)$ there is a natural comparison map $g_!Rf'_*K\to Rf_*g'_!K$ in $D(Y_{\acute et},\Lambda)$, where the quasi-finite lower shriek $g_!,g'_!$ is exact. This map is an isomorphism **under either alternative separately**: (a) $K$ is bounded below and all $H^i(K)$ are torsion, or (b) $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring.

\label{lemma-shriek-lqf-and-proper}
Consider a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[r]_f \ar[rd]_g & Y \ar[d]^h \\
& Z
}
$$
with $f$ and $g$ locally quasi-finite and $h$ proper. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Funtorially in $K \in D(X_\etale, \Lambda)$ there is a canonical map
$$
g_!K \longrightarrow Rh_*(f_!K)
$$
in $D(Z_\etale, \Lambda)$. This map is an isomorphism if
(a) $K$ is bounded below and has torsion cohomology sheaves, or
(b) $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring.
statement: Consider a commutative triangle of schemes $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ and $g=h\circ f:X\to Z$, with $f$ and $g$ locally quasi-finite and $h$ proper. For any ring $\Lambda$ and $K\in D(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$, there is a canonical natural map $g_!K\to Rh_*(f_!K)$ in $D(Z_{\acute et},\Lambda)$. It is an isomorphism if either (a) $K$ is bounded below with torsion cohomology sheaves or (b) $\Lambda$ is torsion; the two alternatives are not simultaneous hypotheses.
